chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a newborn born on the night of Eid al-Fitr, is Zakat al-Fitr due upon him? He said, 'No, the month has passed.' And I asked him about a Jew who converted to Islam on the night of Eid al-Fitr, is Zakat al-Fitr due upon him? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.فِطْرَةٌ: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْفِطْرِ: The night of Eid al-Fitr, marking the end of Ramadan

ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic principle of temporal precision in Zakat al-Fitr, where the obligation is tied strictly to the presence of Ramadan. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that since the month had already concluded at the time of birth or conversion, the prerequisite condition for the levy was not met. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the exact timing of religious obligations relative to the lunar calendar.
